metadata.title: Follows the File, Not Its Own Reasoning.
metadata.subtitle: The Comps-Analysis Skill (Anthropic Skills)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: when Claude runs an Anthropic Skill like comps-analysis, does it reason its way through the task like an analyst, or does it execute a written file, step by step? Take the mechanism apart — the folder, the SKILL.md, the Steps section, the linear execution — and land the trade-off the design makes: repeatability at the expense of improvisation. Carry-out: inside a Skill, Claude runs the file, not its own reasoning.

beats.narration_text: Here's the wrong guess — thinking Claude reasons its way through a comps analysis, the way an analyst would open the model and think. It doesn't. Inside a Skill, Claude reads a written file, then runs each step in the order it's written. Here's what that actually is.

beats.narration_text: Here's what a Skill actually is: a folder Claude reads before it does anything. This one is called comps-analysis. Inside sits a file called SKILL.md — the full instruction set, written in plain English, no hidden logic and no compiled code. Claude opens the file, reads it, then acts. The design call is the unusual part — they chose text as the runtime, not code. The file itself is the program.

The actual pipeline lives in the file's Steps section. Claude reads each step and runs it, one at a time, in the exact order written. Linear execution — no branching unless a step tells it to branch. They optimized for repeatability at the expense of improvisation. That's the whole trade-off, sitting right on the page.

This is what makes comps-analysis a specification rather than a suggestion. Feed it the same input twice and the same steps produce the same output, both times. This works if you value repeatability and audit trails. It fails if you need Claude to notice something the file didn't anticipate. Step outside what the file actually says, and there's nothing written down to fall back on.

production_viz.label: SPEC, NOT SUGGESTION
production_viz.caption: repeatable — but only inside the file

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening: inside a Skill, Claude executes the written steps — it doesn't reason its own way through the task. Same input, same output, every time. Never more than the file says.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt — paste it into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. I'm about to value a small private company using comparable-companies analysis. Act as my first-pass analyst: walk me through the comps-analysis method step by step — what to select, what to measure, and where the real judgment calls live. Then, using my target company — industry, revenue range, growth stage — propose five public comparables with the specific reason each one is a fair or unfair comp. And name the two multiples that will matter most for this business, and explain why the others matter less here. Go deeper: which of your comparables is closest on the metrics that matter but weakest on business quality — and if you had to explain that trade-off in one sentence to a skeptical CFO, what would it say? Liam, in for Bear.
